The vision screening checks whether your sight meets the required standard of twenty forty, and an applicant who does not meet it is referred, at their own expense, to a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist who evaluates whether any restrictions belong on the driving privilege.

Failing the road test means waiting at least one week before another try, and after a third failed road test the minimum wait rises to one month.

why_how.text: A student who passes a high school instructor's road test gets a Driver Education Examination Certificate, and the license is issued only after that certificate, a valid learner's permit, a parent-signed application, the fees and proof of Vermont residency are handed in at a motor vehicle customer service office.

A junior driver's license is a provisional license: the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles may take it away when your actions show you are an unsafe driver, and it can also be taken away when your parent or guardian withdraws permission for you to drive.

A junior license holder may not drive a vehicle in the course of employment, such as delivering pizza, until the junior license has been held for one year or the holder turns eighteen, whichever comes first, and may never carry passengers for hire.

During the first three months on a junior driver's license the holder must drive alone unless a qualified supervisor is in the front seat, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, and with one present the only passenger limit is the number of safety belts.

The junior license passenger rules move in three steps: driving alone for the first three months, family members during the second three months, and no passenger limit after six months, with the safety belt count capping every step.

During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin transporting family members, and after six months there is no limit on passengers, but at every stage the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts.

No driver may use any portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle, which includes reading and manually composing or sending texts, instant messages and emails, and the devices covered include cellular phones, personal digital assistants, tablets and laptop computers.

A driver's license is issued to eligible people aged eighteen or older who pass the required examination, and it allows driving any noncommercial vehicle except a school bus or a motorcycle, each of which needs additional exams.

For the full license road test a permit holder brings a qualified supervisor whose license is valid that day, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, plus proof of insurance and registration for a sound, inspected vehicle with a working parking brake.

why_how.text: To get a junior driver's license you must have held a learner's permit for at least one year and kept a clean record with no permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before applying.
The one year a learner's permit must be held before a junior license is a different clock from the six month clean record period, which counts only the six months immediately before applying.
A junior driver's license is issued to a sixteen or seventeen year old who passes the required examination, and a parent or legal guardian must sign the application to give permission for the test.

Before getting a license, every sixteen and seventeen year old must pass a state approved driver education and training course made up of thirty hours of classroom study, six hours of behind the wheel training and six hours of observation.

On top of the driver education course, a junior license applicant must complete forty hours of driving practice with at least ten hours at night, and nighttime means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise.

An applicant may take the road test on a learner's permit that has been expired for no more than three years and was renewed before the exam, but a permit expired for more than three years requires a written exam before the road test can be given.

Driver education taken outside Vermont counts only if a certified or licensed driver education instructor taught it with both classroom and behind the wheel training, and a completion certificate not issued by a state agency needs documentation on state letterhead listing the program's minimum requirements.

A parent or guardian must certify the forty hours of practice driving, at least ten of them at night, using the Driving Practice Log Sheet or the RoadReady app, and the law requires those forty hours to be in addition to the six behind the wheel hours of driver education.
The forty hours of certified practice driving are counted separately from the six behind the wheel hours of the driver education course, so the two never overlap.

Vermont issues six kinds of license: the learner's permit, the driver's license, the junior driver's license, the commercial driver's license, the enhanced driver's license and the driver's privilege card.

A Vermont resident must be at least fifteen years old to take the learner's permit test, and a resident of another state who is enrolled in a Vermont driver education and training course can also get a Vermont learner's permit with a school letter confirming enrollment.

A permit applicant who is fifteen, sixteen or seventeen needs a parent or legal guardian to sign the application before taking the test unless the applicant is an emancipated minor, and a foreign exchange student uses a Foreign Exchange Parental Authorization form that a host parent cannot sign.

A learner's permit applicant under eighteen must have kept a clean driving record for the previous two years, and anyone with recalls, suspensions or revocations should contact the DMV because an additional waiting period may be required.

With a valid learner's permit you may drive anywhere in Vermont at any time, provided the front seat holds a qualified supervisor: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, an unimpaired licensed or certified driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old.
Before driving in another state on a Vermont learner's permit, check with that state's motor vehicle agency or its law enforcement whether the permit is honored there.

title.text: Road test vehicle and paperwork requirements

why_how.text: The vehicle brought to a junior license road test must be clean, in good mechanical condition, legal, carry a valid inspection sticker and have a properly working emergency or parking brake, and failing to show a valid insurance card and registration certificate prevents testing.

The insurance card shown at a road test must state the name of the insurance carrier, the effective and expiration dates of coverage, the name of the insured and a description of the vehicle including its vehicle identification number.

A school bus with a gross vehicle weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, requires a commercial driver's license with passenger and school bus endorsements.

A Type Two school bus endorsement on a regular license covers buses rated for fewer than sixteen passengers, while sixteen or more passengers or a heavy weight rating moves the driver into commercial licensing with passenger and school bus endorsements.

A school bus endorsement is required to transport school children for hire, such as in a taxi, or in a multifunction school activity bus owned or leased by a school, and may also be required when carrying school children in privately or school owned cars and vans.

Any licensed person aged sixteen or older may get a motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit by passing a test, and students who complete the Basic Rider Course of the Vermont Rider Education Program are exempt from the state written and skill exams for the endorsement.

All DMV visits are by appointment only, scheduled through the DMV website, and an applicant who cannot keep an appointment should cancel or reschedule as soon as possible so the time can go to someone else.

You must furnish a registered, inspected and insured vehicle for the road test from any state, a rental vehicle is accepted only when the rental company provides a letter accepting full responsibility, and a vehicle on dealer registration is accepted only for an immediate family member of the dealership.
No road test is given in a vehicle displaying agriculture, antique or exhibit plates, because the law restricts how those plates may be used.

A road test vehicle needs working headlights, horn, wipers, rearview mirror, tail lights, tires, steering, windshield, exhaust, brakes, fenders and bumpers, plus directional signals on vehicles made after the start of nineteen fifty-five and safety belts and defrosters on models from nineteen sixty-four on.

The emergency or parking brake of a road test vehicle must be able to hold it in neutral on any grade where it is operated, both headed uphill and downhill, and illegal tinting of the front windows is not allowed.
Carrying school children in a school bus the manufacturer rates for fewer than sixteen passengers requires a Type Two school bus endorsement on the regular driver's license.
No road test is given in a vehicle that does not have safety belts.
